ruling.recommended_action: Refund S$1.18 (approx.) to the rider as a Ryde voucher for the unexempted second detour, and send the driver's account for review of a repeated route-deviation pattern (+ flag_account).
ruling.reasoning:
Service is RydeTAXI (metered): any unexempted detour km enters the fare, so RD-2 applies with the metered distance rate = distance_fare ÷ distance_km = 30.54 ÷ 21.66 = S$1.41/km.

Safety screen: chat contains only a route request and a one-word agreement; the driver's statement is factual rerouting; no threat, abuse, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation anywhere. safety_concern = none.

Two off-route segments are visible in the trace, matching the rider's own account ("jam near the start" + "a second time without asking"):

seg1 (≈17:01:30–17:06:30, Bedok North area, PIE slip-road loop, rejoining at ≈1.3360,103.9334): the driver asked at 17:01:25 ("ok if I go round via Bedok North Road?") and the rider replied at 17:02:05 ("Sure, your call.") — before the segment's driving loops fully began. The segment itself is partly covered by a standing LTA band-4 record on PIE (SYN-0009) in the trip window, but the traffic record is ambiguous as evidence (no band-1/2 confirmation of the substituted route), so I rest the exemption on the rider's own consent: a named-road agreement where the trace's standing/loops in the Bedok North Road corridor tie the driven segment to the named road (RD-5). Exempt.

seg2 (≈17:21:30–17:24:30, the northbound loop around 1.3106/1.3125→1.3148/1.3231, peaking ≈1.3 km north of the dropoff corridor): no rider message before it; the driver's only explanation is "my GPS rerouting", which is not a rider consent and not a documented reasonable cause (no incident on the optimal route, no band 1/2). It is a driver/route-choice detour that the 17:02:05 "your call" does not cover (that agreement was scoped only to getting round the jam near the start, and no message ties this later loop to any agreed road). It counts as an unexempted detour (RD-1, RD-5, G13).

Amount: the trace is thinned (1 sample ≈ 290 m at ~35 km/h), so segment extra-km is estimated with that uncertainty. seg2 adds roughly 1.5 km of forward detour beyond the roughly straight 19.0 km covered kilometres (dense polyline ≈16.3 km), while the metered distance is 21.66 km — i.e. ≈1.6–1.9 km of metre-recorded excess beyond the nominal route, almost all of it explained by seg2 (seg1 being a same-road slip loop). Using the conservatively low end of the estimate: ≈0.84 extra_km × 1.41/km ≈ S$1.18. RydeTAXI, so the refund is the meter distance units only; any non-metered top-up on that segment is outside the policy's calculation. The metered waiting_fee (S$0.13) is waiting time under RD-3(c) and is not refundable.

Driver profile: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 2 (with this case, "repeated"), so RD-6 attaches flag_account; the profile was used only as the basis for that additional action, not to decide the detour.

segment_findings.reason: Driver asked before the detour (17:01:25) whether he could go round via Bedok North Road and the rider agreed (17:02:05 'Sure, your call.'), i.e. a named-road agreement made before the segment; the driver's trace (standing at 1.3376,103.9331 and loops in the 1.3360,103.9334 corridor, rejoining the optimal route at ≈17:06:30) ties the driven segment to the named road. Exempt under RD-5. PIE band 4 (SYN-0009) in the trip window is corroborative only; RD-4(b) does not exempt on its own.

No rider message before the second detour; the driver's only explanation is 'my GPS rerouting'. A general 'your call' given at 17:02:05 covers the route chosen to get round the jam near the start, not a later northbound loop that goes ≈1.3 km north of the dropoff corridor (1.3106/1.3125 → 1.3148/1.3231) before turning back south. No incident on the optimal route and no band 1/2, so no reasonable cause. Counts under RD-1/RD-5.

rejected_claims.reason: The driver says the second turn-off was his GPS rerouting; RD-5 requires the rider's own pre-detour message consenting to that segment, and no such message exists between 17:02:05 and the 17:21:30 segment. A GPS reroute is not a rider agreement, and the 17:02:05 'your call' cannot be stretched to cover an unspecified later loop.
No traffic incident on the optimal route in the record (incidents: []), and the available speed band is band 4 on PIE; RD-4(a)/(b) therefore do not exempt the second segment.

ruling.evidence_gap: Trace is thinned to 30 s samples (≈290 m spacing); segment extra-km is an estimate from the polyline and metered distance, stated as an uncertainty band, not a missing record.
